오늘 챙겨야 할 해외 이슈

1) 미 장기금리 24년래 고점 재테스트(10년물 ~5.30%, 30년물 ~5.65%) 왜 지금: 8월 PCE가 예상보다 낮았고 10월 금리인상 확률도 약 35~40%로 낮아졌지만, Q2 GDP 상향(2.2%)과 민간 최종수요 견조, 대규모 회사채 발행 등으로 장기물 금리가 뛰며 주식이 장중 반등 후 되밀렸다. 글로벌 채권도 최근 분기 중 가장 약했고, 달러는 월간 강세·엔화는 BOJ 요약 이후 약세를 보였다. 장기금리 상승은 글로벌 자금조달비용·밸류에이션·크레딧 스프레드 전반에 파급될 수 있어 추세 관찰이 필요하다. 2) 물가 둔화(코어 PCE 3.0% YoY, 0.2% MoM)와 소비 견조(실질 +0.6%)의 엇갈림 왜 지금: 헤드라인 PCE 3.4%로 기대보다 낮았지만, 소비지출은 탄탄하고(명목 +0.9%), 저축률은 4.6%→4.1%로 하락, 소비자신뢰는 12년반 만의 저점권으로 상반된 신호를 준다. 시장은 단기 추가인상 기대를 낮췄지만(10월 확률 하락), 연말 재인상 가능성은 열어둔 상태다. 이 조합은 연준의 “높고 오래” 스탠스, 미 달러·금리 경로, 주식·원자재 변동성에 직접 연결된다. 3) 유가 재상승과 중동 리스크(브렌트 ~$103.5, WTI ~$90.4), 재고 감소 왜 지금: 미-이란 협상 교착과 휘발유(-170만배럴)·디젤(-230만배럴) 재고 감소가 겹치며 유가가 반등했다. 에너지 가격은 근원물가 파급이 제한적이더라도 기대인플레이션·기간프리미엄을 자극해 장기금리와 크레딧·주식 리스크 프리미엄에 영향을 줄 수 있다. 지정학 경로 의존도가 높아 추세 추종 관점에서 가격·변동성의 지속 여부를 확인할 필요가 있다. 4) 연준 커뮤니케이션: “신중하되 필요시 추가긴축” 톤과 장기요인(에너지·AI 수요) 왜 지금: 윌리엄스는 9월 인상 후 긴급성은 낮지만 2026년 후반 25bp 추가 가능성을 언급했고, 무살렘·굴즈비·바르는 공급충격(에너지 등) 지속 시 더 높은 금리를 시사했다. 윌리엄스는 유가와 AI 수요가 장기금리(기간프리미엄) 상방 요인이라고도 했다. 정책 시그널은 단기 인상확률과 달러/엔, 장단기 금리구조, 성장주/가치주 민감도에 광범위한 영향을 준다. 5) 고용·경기 이벤트 대기: ADP(+9만) 이후 NFP·PMI, AI·설비투자 모멘텀 왜 지금: ADP가 예상을 웃돌았고, 시장은 NFP(이번 주)와 제조업 지표를 대기 중이다. Q2 GDP 상향(2.2%)은 소비와 AI 관련 설비투자가 견인했다는 점이 강조됐다. 새 데이터는 10월/연말 금리 경로, 장단기 금리 레벨, 달러 강도, 주식 팩터 로테이션(메가캡/AI와 경기민감)의 민감도를 다시 가격에 반영하게 만드는 촉매다.

Carryover stocks down ~20m YoY to 289m. - Price signals: potential upside pressure on prices toward winter due to tighter supplies, despite some futures softness driven by geopolitical uncertainty (Ukraine/Middle East peace dynamics currently weighing on Chicago and London wheat futures). - UK context: AHDB harvest estimates show weakened yields (winter wheat ~6.9 t/ha, spring barley ~4.8 t/ha, oats ~4.6 t/ha; quality issues in malting barley). Local prices softer recently (UK ex-farm feed wheat ~£198.5/t as of late September). - Oilseeds: soybeans expected to reach a record ~440m tonnes globally; stocks trimmed modestly to 73m tonnes due to demand. UK rapeseed yields forecast ~4 t/ha (9% above 5-year average); ex-farm price around £449.4/t, slight weekly decline. Overall outlook for agricultural commodities: tighter grain supplies under El Niño could support higher prices as we approach winter, though near-term futures prices show sensitivity to geopolitical developments. Oilseeds remain robust in production, with favorable domestic rapeseed yields supporting activity, while malting barley quality pressures add complexity to UK grain values.

FAO Cereal Supply and Demand Brief | MTS Insights
www.mtsinsights.com · 2026-10-02T00:00:00.000Z

Summary: - FAO project for global cereal production in 2026 lowered by 3.4 million tonnes since July, to 2,980 Mt, about 2.0% below 2025 and the largest annual drop since 2018, though still the second-largest harvest on record. - Maize outlook: global maize production now 1,309 Mt, down 0.6% from June; declines centered in the EU due to heat/drought (notably France and Poland). Smaller reductions in India and Paraguay; Argentina and Brazil are expected to offset losses with above-average yields. - Rice: world rice production forecast at 553.1 Mt (milled basis) in 2026/27, down 1.9% from 2025/26, pressured by tighter margins and El Niño-related weather. - Wheat outlook: revisions show some gains offset by downgrades (specifics not fully detailed in highlights); notable improvements in Argentina/Brazil, offsets from China/Philippines and a larger cut for the United States where plantings are at multi-decade lows. - Global cereal trade (2026/27 Jul/Jun): raised slightly to 509.3 Mt (+0.3%), driven by stronger maize trade and US/export activity; Argentina projected to export up to 39.0 Mt, nearing Brazil’s level. Europe’s import needs anticipated to rise due to lower production. Uncertainty persists around Black Sea export flows (Russia/Ukraine) due to logistics and route diversification. - Rice trade (2026 calendar year): raised to 60.5 Mt, supported by higher expectations for the Philippines, but overall world rice trade still expected to fall about 1.9% from the 2025 peak. Implications for agricultural commodities market: - Maize remains the main drag on overall cereal production due to EU heat/drought; watch EU crop conditions and feed demand. - Wheat and rice near-term prospects depend on weather and Black Sea logistics, with some regional upside (Argentina/Brazil) and ongoing diversification pressures. - Global cereal trade remains below record 2025/26 levels despite modest gains, suggesting tighter balance and potential price volatility, especially for maize and rice. - Policy and weather risk (El Niño impacts) remain key drivers for 2026 outlook.

El Niño could push Peru's agricultural export losses to $1.5B - FreshFruitPortal.com
www.freshfruitportal.com · 2026-09-29T00:00:00.000Z

Summary: - A severe El Niño is forecast for Peru’s 2026-27 summer (Dec–Mar), with the heaviest agricultural export losses expected in 2027. - Preciso Consultoría estimates Peru’s top 20 farm exports could drop by 969,000 tons and FOB value by about $1.498 billion across 2026–2027 vs a no-El Niño scenario. - In 2026, top exports could be 7% below no-El Niño levels; in 2027, about 14% below. Export value in 2027 could be around $11.3B vs $12.4B without El Niño. Prices may rise modestly (from $2.61 to $2.75/kg) but not fully offset the lost volume, leaving ~9% lower value than the no-El Niño baseline. - Heat-sensitive crops suffer most: mango production could fall to 178,595 tons (vs 557,440 normally), with mango volumes ~49% below trend in 2027. Table grapes could be ~4% below trend in 2027. - Regional impacts: the northern coast (high rainfall) could lose $458M in 2027; the rest of the country faces about $639M in losses, mainly due to extreme heat and drought rather than rain. - Key takeaway: 2027 is the critical year; higher prices will not fully offset the loss of volume. Source: USDA Market News via Agronometrics. If you want, I can extract a concise sector-by-sector forecast or compare this outlook with prior El Niño episodes.

Fertiliser affordability pressure despite easing supply risks | Eyre Peninsula Advocate
epadvocate.com.au · 2026-09-25T00:00:00.000Z

Rabobank’s semi-annual fertiliser outlook notes that global fertiliser markets are easing from the sharp supply disruptions seen earlier, but affordability remains a major challenge for farmers through 2027. Key points: - Prices for fertilisers have risen faster than agricultural commodities, keeping affordability negative across major regions despite some improvement. - Demand has softened due to higher costs, with farmers reducing application rates, altering rotations, and shifting to less nitrogen-intensive systems. - Phosphate fertilisers are the hardest hit (supply constraints and higher production costs). Global phosphate demand is projected to contract about 7% in 2026. - Sulphur exports fell ~40% YoY in H1 2026, pushing up phosphate production costs and keeping phosphate prices elevated. - Nitrogen markets show gradual improvement: urea prices eased after initial spikes, with expected global urea demand down ~5% in 2026 before a slow recovery as affordability improves. - Potash remains the most stable nutrient; affordability has weakened slightly but supply disruption has been less severe. - Australian farmers should monitor global grain and oilseed markets. Despite continued geopolitical tensions, shipping disruptions, and weather risks, global crop inventories remain historically high, easing some supply/demand shocks. - Risks over the next 6–12 months include El Niño impacts on crop production, rising farm input costs, and Black Sea export challenges, which could push crop and fertiliser prices higher. Bottom line for agricultural commodities market outlook: while the immediate fertiliser supply risk has eased, cost pressures persist, particularly for phosphate and sulphur, contributing to overall higher input costs. Nitrogen (urea) may rebound gradually as affordability improves, while potash remains relatively steadier. Global grain/oilseed prices and stocks remain a critical backdrop for demand and price direction.

Allendale’s Rich Nelson Analyzes USDA Small Grains Summary and Quarterly Grain Stocks - Oklahoma Farm Report
wpengine · 2026-09-30T00:00:00.000Z

Summary: Allendale’s Rich Nelson, with Farm Director KC Sheperd, analyzes USDA quarterly grain stocks and the Small Grains Summary to frame the current agricultural commodities outlook. Key takeaways: - Wheat: 2026 U.S. all-wheat production revised up to about 1.534 billion bushels, but stronger-than-expected first-quarter disappearance supports prices. Sept 1 wheat stocks at 1.85 billion bu vs. 1.87 billion expected. With favorable domestic use but no new export catalyst, producers with stored hard red winter wheat should consider pricing now; a Kansas City wheat value around $6.25–$6.50 with a ~15% protein premium over corn. - Corn: Old-crop stocks ~2.1 billion bu, higher than trade estimates, expanding the new-crop carry to roughly 1.7–1.8 billion bu. December futures could hover near $5.10 on theoretical balance but may drop toward $4.75 due to lagging new-crop exports and fading feed usage late in the year. - Soybeans: Sept 1 supplies ~315 million bu, down 10 million from expectations, tightening the new-crop balance toward ~300 million bu. However, current cash/futures prices are already above levels suggested by the tighter stocks, pressured by uncertain export demand, especially potential hesitancy from China on commitments (possible 25 million tons import risk). - Market drivers: Despite some favorable use, overall sentiment has not sustained a supply-driven rally. Export optimism remains tempered by reduced geopolitical risk premiums from the Black Sea, and rainfall in the Southern Plains eases early harvest concerns and acreage worries. - October outlook: Watch (1) Midwest rains delaying harvest and possible quality issues, though unlikely to cause major yield losses; (2) USDA export target revisions in the October 9 S&D report, as ongoing demand weakness could force downward revisions later in the marketing year. Bottom line: The grain complex faces mixed signals—tightening soybean and wheat fundamentals contrast with burdensome corn carry, while export demand and weather developments will be decisive in shaping near-term pricing and marketing decisions. For producers, timely pricing is advised given current levels, with close attention to export commitments and October reports.

DBB기초금속 (Base Metals)매도종가 25.30
추천: 매도 — 종가(25.30)가 트레일링 스탑(25.51)을 하향 돌파했고, 20일·100일 Donchian 상단 돌파도 없으므로 규칙상 청산입니다. 근거 - 기계적 판정: 청산 시그널(종가 < 최근 고점 − 3×ATR)이 True입니다. ATR(14) = 0.30, 트레일링 스탑 = 25.51, 현재 종가 = 25.30으로 스탑 하회. 신규 매수 조건(20일/100일 상단 상향 돌파)은 모두 False이므로 보유 유지/추가 매수 사유가 없습니다. - 뉴스 팩트 체크(추세 또는 청산을 뒷받침하는가): 1) SMM Macro Weekly: 최근 구리 가격이 고점에서 후퇴했고, 단기 방향은 미 연준 금리 경로와 관세 뉴스 대기 모드에 좌우되며 기본 시나리오는 하향 드리프트(LME 14,200–14,650/mt 범위)라고 전합니다. 또한 재고·스프레드와 운송비 이슈로 의미 있는 차익거래가 제한적이라고도 합니다. DBB는 구리 비중이 큰 바스킷이므로, 이와 같은 모멘텀 둔화·하방 바이어스는 스탑 하향 이탈에 대한 합리적 배경을 제공합니다. 2) “Chinese Metals Demand Softens…”: 중국 제조 PMI가 50 이하로 수요가 약하고, 연휴 전 비축으로 프리미엄이 일시적으로 높았으나 연휴 후엔 완화될 가능성이 크다고 짚습니다. 이는 단기 타이트니스가 있더라도 지속적 수요 기반이 취약하다는 뜻으로, 지금의 추세 둔화/청산 신호를 뒷받침합니다. - 보조 참고: Fastmarkets 업데이트는 공급 타이트·재고 낮음 등으로 근시일 내 상방 가능성을 언급하지만, 동시에 금리·주식 변동성 등 거시 역풍을 경고합니다. 신호가 혼재된 뉴스보다 가격이 이미 스탑을 이탈했다는 사실이 우선이며, 규칙상 청산을 번복하지 않습니다. - 일목균형표(구름 위·양운): 보조지표는 우호적이지만 이는 참고용일 뿐입니다. 매도 신호와 엇갈리므로, 재진입 시에는 Donchian 상단 재돌파가 확인될 때 규모를 축소해 분할 진입하는 식으로 리스크를 관리하길 권합니다. 행동 요약 - 지금은 포지션 청산(매도). - 대기: 다음 매수는 종가의 Donchian 상단 상향 돌파가 재확인될 때만. 스탑은 최신 고점 − 3×ATR로 갱신.
